original_question: Do the classes MSJ(2) and MSJ(3) coincide for measure-preserving Z-actions? Here T belongs to MSJ(n) if every ergodic self-joining of n copies of T, other than the product measure mu^{otimes n}, has at least one projection to a two-dimensional face of X x ... x X equal to Delta_{T^i}, the image of the diagonal measure under a power T^i.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in §1: whether the classes MSJ(2) and MSJ(3) coincide for ergodic measure-preserving automorphisms; Proposition 1.2 gives the equivalent reformulation via pairwise-independent 3-fold self-joinings, and Theorem 1.3 records the consequences of a counterexample.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right problem in the paper: the MSJ(2) versus MSJ(3) question for measure-preserving Z-actions generated by a single transformation T. It also captures the correct higher-order MSJ idea, namely that a non-product ergodic n-fold self-joining must have some two-coordinate marginal equal to an off-diagonal joining Δ_{T^i}.
missing_details: The paper is about an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation T, equivalently an ergodic Z-action, on a standard Lebesgue probability space (X, B, μ).
An n-fold self-joining should be stated precisely as a T×...×T-invariant probability measure λ on X^n whose one-coordinate marginals are all μ.
For n=2, the definition specializes to: every ergodic 2-fold self-joining is either μ×μ or an off-diagonal joining Δ_{T^m}.
The off-diagonal joining should be defined explicitly as Δ_{T^m}=(Id×T^m)_*Δ, where Δ=(Id,Id)_*μ and m ranges over Z.
The paper's main question is specifically MSJ(2)=MSJ(3), not the broader question whether MSJ(2)=MSJ(n) for all n.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should spell out that the relevant two-dimensional faces are the pairwise coordinate projections of an n-fold joining.
Proposition 1.2 gives an equivalent reformulation in terms of ergodic 3-fold self-joinings with all pairwise marginals equal to μ×μ; your draft does not mention this paper-explicit equivalence.
No extra algebraic data such as ambient ring, field, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here.
refined_question: Let T be an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation of a standard Lebesgue probability space (X, B, μ). For n≥2, say that T belongs to MSJ(n) if every ergodic self-joining λ of order n, i.e. every ergodic T×...×T-invariant probability measure on X^n with all one-coordinate marginals equal to μ, is either the product measure μ^{⊗ n} or else has at least one two-coordinate marginal equal to an off-diagonal joining Δ_{T^m}=(Id×T^m)_*Δ for some m∈Z, where Δ=(Id,Id)_*μ. Is it true that MSJ(2)=MSJ(3) for ergodic measure-preserving Z-actions (equivalently, ergodic automorphisms T)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as in Proposition 1.2, if T∈MSJ(2), must every ergodic 3-fold self-joining λ of T whose three pairwise coordinate marginals are all μ×μ be the product measure μ×μ×μ?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's principal open problem in the introduction: Conjecture 1.1 asks whether MSJ(2) and MSJ(3) coincide. The draft already has the right object and nearly the right MSJ(n) condition, but it leaves implicit the standard probability-space setting, ergodicity of T, the precise invariant-measure definition of an n-fold self-joining, and the exact definition of the off-diagonal joining Δ_{T^m}. Proposition 1.2 is the key nearby sharpening because it reformulates the conjecture as the nonexistence of a nontrivial ergodic pairwise-independent 3-fold self-joining for a system in MSJ(2). Theorem 1.3 explains why the paper isolates exactly this frontier: a counterexample T in MSJ(2) but not in MSJ(3) would have major dynamical consequences, so the narrow MSJ(2) versus MSJ(3) question is the paper-faithful target rather than a broader higher-order variant.
